[WP] For every day and every night that I've been here; it's been following me.. the eye of a camera.

So I was to start this fancy university in Stockholm, Royal Institute of Technology it was called. A red-brick building complex, with a heavy case of ivy on all the walls. It started with a big party for the newly arrived, zeroes they called us. The party went on to 1 AM.

As I was leaving the building, going through an impressive and really old archway of stone, I saw something move in the corner of my eye. I stopped. It had been like a shadow on the wall of the nearest building, but I couldn't see anything special right now. Just some windows, the ivy, a security camera - pointed straight at me, but that was just a coincidence - nothing moving, nothing special. I stood there for a sec, but then brushed it off and continued walking. Only I saw it again. Now I turned a bit more aggressively towards what I thought I saw. I was sure it had been somewhere around that security camera. A squirrel? A bird? Wait. Why was the camera still pointing at me, after I had moved? As a chill went through my spine, I moved a step to the left. Nothing. Another one... Nothing. But as I walked a few steps more, the fucking thing did turn with my movement. Was someone watching me? Why? Frightened, and not tired at all anymore, I walked with quick steps to my bike, unlocked it and went home. The cam was still tracking me, not even bothering to be secretive anymore.

Next day, approaching school, I was hoping it had all just been a fucked up dream. And it turned out I had all reasons to believe that too: the camera was gone. Weird place to put a security cam anyway. Nothing to watch. So on I went with my studies, to the first lesson. We were about thirty students, densely packed in a relatively small classroom ("the rooms are currently all overbooked due to the new arrivals").

"Kate Newell?"

"Present."

Class was starting. The lecture was interesting, something about studying technique, but something else suddenly caught my attention. There was a wall-mounted camera in the room. Was it really pointed at me, or was it just my general direction? It certainly felt like the former. What followed was a 45 minutes of class, but I just couldn't focus, I had to look up at the camera every once in a while. It was creeping me out. It moved while I was walking out, but only a little jerk.

It went on like this for six months. A little camera would be there at random places, looking at me. Sometimes it went away next time I was there, sometimes not. I spoke with some other students, even some of the staff, but no one paid any mind. "Just a regular camera" is all they would say. So I tried to ignore it; after all, it wasn't doing any harm.

Until today, when it crossed the line.
